skill.name: hol-guard
skill.description: Set up HOL Guard, protect local AI harnesses, review approvals and evidence, and verify plugins, skills, MCP servers, or marketplace packages.
skill.summary: Protect local AI harnesses and verify agent packages with HOL Guard and plugin-scanner.
skill.author: hashgraph-online

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, command fences, and a rule prohibiting .env access. Confirmed findings involve package installation, harness configuration, approval actions, and optional cloud synchronization; these are legitimate features with operational security risk.

remediation.issue: Package installation examples do not pin versions or document artifact verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions and instruct users to verify the publisher and package integrity before installation.

remediation.issue: Bootstrap and install commands can change local harness hooks or configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Require a dry run, show the planned changes, and obtain explicit user confirmation before applying harness modifications.

remediation.issue: Approval commands can authorize work that Guard blocked.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for each approval and display the risk reason, scope, and request identifier first.

remediation.issue: Cloud synchronization does not state which evidence leaves the machine.
remediation.suggestion: Describe the destination and transmitted fields, then require confirmation before connect or sync operations.

content.user_title: Protect AI Harnesses with HOL Guard
content.value_statement: Local AI harnesses can expose risky tools, plugins, and configuration changes. HOL Guard guides controlled setup, approval review, evidence collection, and package verification.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether hol-guard and plugin-scanner commands are available.
Guides isolated installation through pipx when the user requests setup.
Bootstraps and protects supported local AI harnesses through HOL Guard commands.
Reviews approvals, receipts, inventory, events, and Guard explanations.
Scans plugins, skills, MCP configurations, marketplaces, and mixed agent workspaces.
Runs diagnostics and reports evidence before claiming protection or release readiness.
limitations: Requires the separate hol-guard and plugin-scanner command-line packages.
Cannot prove protection or release readiness without successful command output.
Cloud synchronization details depend on the installed HOL Guard service and configuration.
Does not replace manual review of approval scope, scanner failures, or local changes.

use_cases.title: Protect a developer harness
use_cases.description: Install Guard integration, run a dry check, and verify protection for Codex, Claude Code, or another supported harness.
use_cases.target_user: Software developers using local AI coding tools

use_cases.title: Review blocked tool activity
use_cases.description: Inspect queued approvals, risk reasons, receipts, and configuration differences before deciding whether work may continue.

use_cases.title: Verify an agent package release
use_cases.description: Lint and verify plugins, skills, MCP servers, or marketplace packages before publishing a release.

prompt_templates.title: Check Guard availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether HOL Guard and plugin-scanner are installed. Report availability and recommend isolated installation steps without changing my environment.

prompt_templates.title: Protect one harness
prompt_templates.prompt: Protect my [harness] workspace with HOL Guard. Run a dry check first, explain planned changes, and verify final status with command evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review an approval request
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect Guard request [request-id]. Explain its risk reason and scope, show relevant evidence, and wait for my decision before approving or denying.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a mixed workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this mixed agent workspace. Verify packages, inspect Guard status and evidence, then identify unresolved release risks without claiming readiness prematurely.

output_examples.input: Check whether this Codex workspace is protected.
output_examples.output: HOL Guard detected the Codex workspace. Protection is not confirmed because the status check did not prove an active Guard installation.

output_examples.input: Review the pending Guard approval before I decide.
output_examples.output: The request remains pending. The review identifies its requested scope, risk reason, related configuration difference, and available receipt evidence.

output_examples.input: Verify this skill package for release.
output_examples.output: Package verification completed with one unresolved scanner failure. Release readiness is not confirmed until that failure is inspected and resolved.

best_practices: Run dry checks before applying Guard integration changes.
Review risk reasons and scope before approving queued work.
Use command evidence before reporting protection or release readiness.
anti_patterns: Do not read environment files while diagnosing Guard or scanner behavior.
Do not edit harness configuration directly when a Guard-owned command is available.
Do not ignore scanner failures or approve requests automatically.

faq.question: Does this skill install HOL Guard automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends isolated pipx installation only when setup is requested. Installation still changes the local environment and should use a reviewed version.

faq.question: Does HOL Guard include plugin-scanner?
faq.answer: No. The skill treats hol-guard and plugin-scanner as separate command-line distributions and checks each command independently.

faq.question: Which harnesses are supported?
faq.answer: The documented targets include Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode, and Antigravity.

faq.question: Can the skill approve blocked work?
faq.answer: It documents approval and denial commands. Users should review the risk reason and scope, then explicitly decide each request.

faq.question: What packages can plugin-scanner verify?
faq.answer: It can check Codex plugins, Claude Code projects, skills, MCP server packages, marketplaces, and mixed agent workspaces.

faq.question: How does the skill prove protection?
faq.answer: It uses HOL Guard status, doctor, detection, receipts, inventory, and event evidence. It does not accept configuration presence alone as proof.
